General.Description:
Maria Chen arrived in San Francisco in 1962 with eleven dollars, a steamer trunk, and a pair of worn pointe shoes. She spoke three words of English. By 1981, she was principal dancer with one of the most celebrated ballet companies in the United States. By 1995, she was its artistic director. By the time she retired in 2014, she had transformed American classical dance and mentored a generation of dancers — many of them children of immigrants who saw in her story a reflection of their own.

Biographer James Whitfield spent six years with Maria Chen, conducting hundreds of hours of interviews and gaining unprecedented access to her personal correspondence, rehearsal diaries, and the private photographs that document a life of extraordinary discipline and occasional devastating sacrifice.

A Life in Motion does not shy away from the cost of Chen's achievement: the relationships she could not sustain, the injuries she danced through, the compromises she made and the ones she refused to make. It is a biography of a woman who found in movement a language more honest than words, and who spent sixty years teaching others to speak it.

Whitfield's prose is as precisely crafted as the subject it honours. A superb and moving work.
